title: Sepsis and septic shock: initial resuscitation

sources.title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026 (SCCM/ESICM; Prescott H, et al. Crit Care Med, doi:10.1097/CCM.0000000000007075)

2024 Focused Update: Guidelines on Use of Corticosteroids in Sepsis, ARDS, and Community-Acquired Pneumonia (SCCM; Chaudhuri D, et al. Crit Care Med 2024;52(5):e219-e233, doi:10.1097/CCM.0000000000006172)
ESICM guidelines on circulatory shock and hemodynamic monitoring 2025 (ESICM; Monnet X, et al. Intensive Care Med)

q_shock.text: Sepsis suspected. Is there shock (hypotension or signs of hypoperfusion)?

q_likely.text: No shock. How likely is infection?

q_hypoperf.text: After the initial crystalloid boluses, is the patient still hypoperfused?

q_responsive.text: Fluid responsive on a dynamic test (passive leg raise, pulse pressure variation, stroke volume change)?

q_map.text: Is MAP below target (65 mmHg; 60-65 if age 65 or older)?

q_cardiac.text: Echo: cardiac dysfunction, with hypoperfusion despite adequate volume and MAP?

q_source.text: Source needing control (abscess, obstruction, necrotic tissue, infected line or device)?

e_probable.title: Probable sepsis, no shock
actions: Give antimicrobials immediately, ideally within 1 hour of recognition.
Blood cultures (standard practice, not from the cited guideline); do not let them delay antimicrobials.
Measure lactate; repeat if raised.
Monitor closely for progression to shock.
cautions: Empiric regimen per local antibiogram and protocol.
Beta-lactams: after a loading dose, give maintenance as prolonged infusion (SSC 2026).
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_possible.title: Possible sepsis, no shock
actions: Do a rapid, time-limited assessment for infection and other diagnoses.
If concern for infection persists, start antimicrobials within 3 hours of when sepsis was first suspected.
Measure lactate.
Reassess often; if shock develops, treat as septic shock (antimicrobials immediately).
cautions: Document the time sepsis was first suspected; the 3-hour window counts from then.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_low.title: Low likelihood of infection, no shock
actions: SSC 2026 suggests deferring antimicrobials while monitoring closely.
Look for and treat the alternative diagnosis.
Re-enter this pathway if infection becomes more likely or shock develops.
cautions: Set a clear time for reassessment.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_morefluid.title: Still hypoperfused and fluid responsive
actions: Confirm antimicrobials were given within 1 hour of shock recognition.
Give a further crystalloid bolus; balanced crystalloid preferred over 0.9% saline.
Initial target: at least 30 mL/kg crystalloid in the first 3 hours, individualised (SSC 2026).
If BMI is over 30, base volume on adjusted or ideal body weight.
Reassess with capillary refill, serial lactate and a dynamic test after each bolus.
cautions: Beyond 30 mL/kg, SSC 2026 allows either a liberal or restrictive approach: choose by patient factors.
Do not use starches; gelatin is not suggested.
Albumin is not routine; consider after large crystalloid volumes or in cirrhosis.
Start vasopressor early if MAP stays low; do not wait for fluids to finish.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_vasopressor.title: Septic shock: start vasopressor
actions: Start norepinephrine (first line).
Peripheral start is acceptable; do not delay for a central line.
Target MAP 65 mmHg, titrated within about 5 mmHg; 60-65 if age 65 or older.
Arterial line as soon as practical.
Confirm antimicrobials given within 1 hour of recognition.
IV corticosteroids are suggested in septic shock (dose per local protocol).
cautions: If norepinephrine is escalating: go to the pathway Vasopressor and inotrope escalation (vasopressin next).
Avoid high-dose short steroid courses (over 400 mg/day hydrocortisone-equivalent for under 3 days).
Peripheral vasopressor: no guideline limit on dose, duration or site; follow local policy and check the site often.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_inotrope.title: Septic shock with cardiac dysfunction
actions: Add dobutamine to norepinephrine, or use epinephrine alone (SSC 2026 suggestion).
Recheck volume status and perfusion markers after each change.
Consider cardiac output monitoring (ESICM 2025).
Consider IV corticosteroid per local protocol if not already started.
cautions: Evidence is very low certainty.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_source.title: Source control needed
actions: Arrange source control early, ideally within 6 hours of diagnosis.
Possibly infected line or device: plan removal with the team per local protocol.
If MAP is below target (65 mmHg; 60-65 if age 65 or older), start norepinephrine first line; peripheral start is acceptable (SSC 2026). Dose per local infusion chart.
Continue resuscitation and antimicrobials during the procedure.
IV corticosteroids suggested if in septic shock (dose per local protocol).
cautions: Agree the approach (drainage vs surgery) with the surgical or IR team.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

e_continue.title: Continue resuscitation and review
actions: Confirm antimicrobials within 1 hour; review choice with cultures and local antibiogram.
If MAP is below target (65 mmHg; 60-65 if age 65 or older), start norepinephrine first line; peripheral start is acceptable (SSC 2026). Dose per local infusion chart.
Serial lactate and capillary refill to guide further fluid (not 'fluid until lactate normal').
Keep looking for a source that needs control.
If on vasopressors: IV corticosteroids suggested (dose per local protocol).
Once stable, plan active fluid removal to avoid overload.
cautions: De-escalate antimicrobials once organism and sensitivities are known.
Routine empiric antifungal cover is not suggested without risk factors.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.

q_bundle.text: Shock. Antimicrobials given and initial crystalloid started?

e_bundle.title: Septic shock: first steps now
actions: Give antimicrobials immediately if not already given, ideally within 1 hour of recognising shock (SSC 2026).
Blood cultures (standard practice, not from the cited guideline); do not let them delay antimicrobials.
Measure lactate; repeat it to guide resuscitation.
Start crystalloid: at least 30 mL/kg IV in the first 3 hours, individualised; balanced crystalloid preferred over 0.9% saline.
If BMI is over 30, base volume on adjusted or ideal body weight.
If MAP stays below target, start norepinephrine peripherally; do not wait for central access.
Then re-enter this pathway and answer 'Yes, both'.
cautions: Reassess after each bolus; capillary refill time is a useful adjunct (SSC 2026).
Empiric regimen per local antibiogram and protocol.
Verify doses against local formulary/protocol.
